opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and new commerce and AI features. Down 27% YoY, from $458M a year ago.

opex.note: Losses on merchant loans and cash advances, and transaction losses. Up 21% YoY as more sales flowed through Shopify Payments.

follow100Note: Subscription plans bring in $27.46 of every $100 and merchant solutions $72.54 — mostly a cut of merchants' sales. Direct costs take $48.58 and running the business takes another $46.80, leaving $4.62 of operating profit per $100. But a $373M paper loss on investments and a $44M loss on the Flexport stake overwhelmed it: after $17M of tax, Shopify lost $14.67 of every $100. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: The earnings release prints a condensed statement (operating income $86M, total other expense $342M, net loss $273M); the split of that $342M into interest income, the unrealized investment loss, the equity-method loss and the foreign-exchange loss comes from the detailed interim financial statements in Exhibit 99.1 of the same Form 6-K, as the release itself directs.
oneTimers: $373M unrealized loss on equity and other investments — mostly a $351M drop in the value of investments with readily determinable fair values as their share prices fell during the quarter (including a $16M unrealized loss on Shopify's option to buy Klaviyo shares). Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $256M (non-GAAP) versus a $273M GAAP net loss.
$44M net loss on Shopify's equity-method investment in Flexport.

Stock-based compensation of $105M — a non-cash expense inside operating expenses ($68M in R&D, $25M in G&A, $11M in sales and marketing, plus $1M in cost of revenues). It is recurring, not one-off, but it is paid in shares rather than cash, so it does not reduce the $232M of free cash flow Shopify generated.
otherDetail: Other expense of $342M in total: a $373M unrealized loss on equity and other investments and a $4M foreign-exchange loss, partly offset by $79M of interest income. The $44M equity-method loss is the separate equityM line; the rest nets to otherIncomeM of -$298M.
pngFooterNote: Operating profit is back — investment losses made it a net loss.

segments.name: Subscription solutions
segments.note: The monthly plans merchants pay to run their stores on Shopify. Up 34% YoY; monthly recurring revenue reached $151M.

segments.name: Merchant solutions
segments.note: Mostly payment processing (Shopify Payments) — a cut of the sales flowing through merchants' stores — plus shipping and other merchant services. Up 20% YoY and 73% of all revenue.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 23% to $1.86B as GMV grew 23% to $60.9B — 29% after adjusting for the sale of the logistics businesses. Subscription revenue grew 34% to $511M on more merchants and higher plan prices, with monthly recurring revenue up 32% to $151M, while merchant solutions rose 20% to $1.35B as Shopify Payments processed 60% of GMV ($36.2B).
takeaways.title: Growth stayed strong

takeaways.text: Operating income was $86M (5% margin) versus a $193M loss a year ago. On an adjusted basis, operating income was $201M (11% margin) versus an adjusted loss of $31M, and gross margin widened to 51.4% from 47.5% as the dilutive logistics business exited. Free cash flow more than doubled to $232M, a 12% margin versus 6% a year ago.
takeaways.title: Operating profit returned

takeaways.text: Net income was a $273M loss despite the operating profit: a $373M unrealized loss on equity investments — mostly a $351M drop in listed holdings as share prices fell — plus a $44M loss on the Flexport stake, partly offset by $79M of interest income. Excluding equity investments, adjusted net income was $256M versus $12M a year ago.
takeaways.title: Investment losses turned profit into a net loss

verdict: Shopify grew revenue 23% to $1.9B and returned to an $86M operating profit — but a $373M paper loss on its investments swung the quarter to a $273M net loss.
